Early in the morning, you will be transferred to the port of Buenos Aires. You will cross the Río de la Plata estuary by ferry and arrive in Montevideo, where the tour begins directly from the port.

The itinerary includes the Port of Montevideo, Independence Square, the city center, the Old Town and the Cathedral. Independence Square is home to the mausoleum of José Gervasio Artigas and the Art Deco Palacio Salvo.

After the sightseeing tour, you will have some free time. You will then return to Buenos Aires by ferry, followed by a transfer to your hotel on arrival.

Colonia del Sacramento was founded by the Portuguese in 1680 and is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The town was long disputed by Portugal and Spain, and in 1777 it finally came under Spanish rule.

The walking portion of the excursion begins at Plaza Mayor. The route continues along the Street of Sighs to the Basilica of the Blessed Sacrament and San Pedro Bastion. You will then climb the lighthouse for a panoramic view of the town; on a clear day, the port of Buenos Aires can be seen from here.

If you wish, you can visit the Tile Museum, the Archaeological Museum and other local museums. The itinerary also includes Real de San Carlos, the Chapel of St. Benedict the Moor and Granja Arenas, which houses a Guinness World Records collection of pencils.

After the main part of the excursion, there is free time to buy souvenirs, have lunch or stroll along the waterfront and the streets of the historic center.

Xel-Há is located on the Riviera Maya. In the park, you can snorkel among tropical fish, explore the jungle on foot, ride a bicycle or mini-train and observe the local flora and fauna.

The excursion is offered on an all-inclusive basis. After the activities, you can have lunch at one of the park's four restaurants.

Tigre lies approximately 40 km from Buenos Aires, among the islands and waterways of the Río de la Plata delta. The town is often called the Venice of Argentina.

On a sightseeing boat trip, you will see mansions, green parks, restaurants and cafés along the waterfront. The itinerary also includes the San Isidro district, the presidential residence at Quinta de Olivos and the building of the Rowing Club, constructed in the 19th century.

The route from Cusco leads to Machu Picchu. The trip includes a train journey followed by a bus ascent along a winding road to the ancient city, with views of the Urubamba River and its canyon.

At Machu Picchu, you will see terraces, stairways, ceremonial spaces and residential areas of the Inca city. The stone structures stand among mountain slopes and high-altitude vegetation.

At the scheduled time, the return journey begins, with a train ride and a transfer back to Cusco.
